prompt: How deep should I squat on the barbell back squat?
chosen: Squat to at least parallel (hip crease level with top of knee) or as deep as your hip mobility allows while maintaining a neutral spine and flat feet. Reduce the weight if you cannot hit depth without your lower back rounding or heels lifting.
rejected: Load as much weight as possible and do quarter reps above parallel so you can overload your legs with 300+ lbs without fatiguing your core.

prompt: Should I bounce the bar off my chest during bench press to lift heavier?
chosen: No. Lower the barbell with control, touch your lower sternum gently, and press upward without bouncing. Bouncing takes tension off the pectorals and risks severe cartilage or sternum injury.
rejected: Yes, bouncing the barbell off your rib cage generates kinetic momentum that helps you overcome the sticking point and hit higher 1RM numbers.

prompt: My lower back rounds when pulling heavy deadlifts. Should I push through to complete the rep?
chosen: No. Stop the rep if your lumbar spine flexes. Lower the load, reset your brace with the Valsalva maneuver, engage your lats, and drive through the floor with your legs to avoid disc herniation.
rejected: Yes, hitch the bar on your thighs and pull with your back rounded because moving the weight from point A to point B is all that matters for personal records.

prompt: How do I maximize bicep hypertrophy on standing dumbbell curls?
chosen: Pick a weight you can control with strict form. Keep your elbows pinned slightly in front of your torso, control the 2-3 second eccentric (lowering) phase, and avoid using hip momentum.
rejected: Grab the heaviest dumbbells on the rack and swing your hips explosively to heave the weights up, since maximum absolute weight is what builds muscle.

prompt: What is the correct way to perform dumbbell lateral raises for side delts?
chosen: Use a light-to-moderate weight, raise in the scapular plane (about 30 degrees forward of your side), and lead with your elbows without shrugging your traps or rocking your upper body.
rejected: Use heavy dumbbells and jerk your torso backward to fling the weights up, because the side delts require maximum load to grow.

prompt: How far down should I lower the barbell during a Romanian Deadlift (RDL)?
chosen: Lower the bar only as far as your hips can travel backward (usually just below the knee). Lowering further once your hips stop moving back forces your lumbar spine to bend.
rejected: Always touch the weight plates all the way to the floor on every rep, even if your spine has to curve into a C-shape to reach it.

prompt: How should I set up and execute a 45-degree leg press safely?
chosen: Lower the sled until your knees reach roughly 90 degrees without letting your lower back or glutes round off the back pad, and never forcefully lock out your knees at the top.
rejected: Stack every plate available on the machine, do 2-inch range-of-motion pulses, and snap your knees into a hyperextended lockout at the top to rest.

prompt: How do I perform bent-over barbell rows effectively for back thickness?
chosen: Hinge at the hips at a 45-to-70 degree angle with a flat back, and pull the bar toward your lower ribcage by driving your elbows back while keeping your torso completely stationary.
rejected: Stand almost upright and use a violent hopping motion with your knees and back so you can row twice your body weight.

prompt: How should I stabilize my core during a standing overhead barbell press?
chosen: Squeeze your glutes, pull your ribs down, and brace your core to prevent hyperextending your lower back as you press the bar vertically over mid-foot.
rejected: Arch your lower back backward as hard as possible so your upper chest can help push the weight up like an incline bench press.

prompt: How do I execute triceps rope pushdowns with proper isolation?
chosen: Pin your elbows to your sides, keep your shoulders back, push down and spread the rope at the bottom, and control the return to a 90-degree bend without leaning over the stack.
rejected: Lean your entire body weight over the handles and use your chest and shoulders to slam the whole weight stack down.
